blocks.text: The Zscaler service provides predefined Data Loss Prevention (DLP) engines:

blocks.item: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
This engine detects Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) violations, using the Social Security Numbers (US) and Medical Information dictionaries.
Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA)
This engine detects violations of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA), using the Social Security Numbers (US) and Financial Statements dictionaries.
Payment Card Industry (PCI)
This engine detects Payment Card Industry (PCI) compliance violations, using the Credit Cards and Social Security Numbers (US) dictionaries.
Offensive Language
This engine detects offensive language, using the Adult Content dictionary.
Self-Harm & Cyberbullying
This engine is intended for use by K-12 educators. If you’re an educator, contact Zscaler Support to enable this feature.
This engine detects violations of student safety, using the Self-Harm & Cyberbullying dictionary.
California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.

The following engines detect California Consumer Privacy Act violations, using the Social Security Numbers (US), Tax Identification Number (US), Names (US), Medical Information, Diseases Information, Drugs Information, and Credit Card dictionaries:
CCPA - High Volume: This engine detects CCPA violations at a high threshold (i.e., more than 25 matches).
CCPA - Low Volume: This engine detects CCPA violations at a low threshold (i.e., more than one match).
Credentials and Secrets
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.
This engine detects credentials and secrets violations, using the Credentials and Secrets dictionary.
Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA)
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.
This engine detects Digital Personal Data Protection Act violations, using the Aadhaar Card Number (India) dictionary.
Finance
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.
This ML-based engine detects financial violations, using the Financial Statements, ABA Bank Routing Number, Credit Cards, and International Bank Account Number (IBAN) dictionaries.
Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA)
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.

The following engines are detect Federal Information Security Modernization Act violations, using the Credit Cards, Diseases Information, Drugs Information, and Social Security Numbers (US) dictionaries:
High Volume: FISMA violations at a high threshold (i.e., more than 25 matches).
Low Volume: FISMA violations at a low threshold (i.e., more than one match).
General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.

The following engines detect General Data Protection Regulation violations, using the Unified Civil Number (Bulgaria), Citizen Service Number (Netherlands), National Economic Registry Number (Poland), National Identification Number (France), National Identification Number (Poland), National Identification Number (Spain), Passport Number (European Union), Social Security Number (Austria), Social Security Number (Spain), Social Security Number (Switzerland), Tax Identification Numbers (Austria), Tax Identification Number (Belgium), Tax Identification Number (Denmark), Tax Identification Number (Finland), Tax Identification Numbers (France), Tax Identification Number (Germany), Tax Identification Number (Greece), Tax Identification Numbers (Hungary), Tax Identification Number (Ireland), Tax Identification Numbers (Luxembourg), Tax Identification Number (Poland), Tax Identification Number (Portugal), Tax Identification Number (Spain), Tax Identification Number (Sweden), Unique Master Citizen Number, VAT Numbers (Austria), VAT Numbers (Belgium), VAT Numbers (France), VAT Numbers (Germany), VAT Number (Ireland), VAT Numbers (Luxembourg), and VAT Numbers (Netherlands) dictionaries:
High Volume: GDPR violations at a high threshold (i.e., more than 25 matches).
Low Volume: GDPR violations at a low threshold (i.e., more than one match).
Legal
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.
This ML-based engine detects legal violations, using the Legal Document dictionary.
General Personal Data Protection Law (LGPD)
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.
The following engines detect General Personal Data Protection Law violations, using the CNPJ Number (Brazil) and Individual Taxpayer Registry ID (Brazil) dictionaries:
High Volume: LGPD violations at a high threshold (i.e., more than 25 matches).
Low Volume: LGPD violations at a low threshold (i.e., more than one match).
Medical
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.

This ML-based engine detects medical violations, using the Medical Information, Diseases Information, Drugs Information, National Provider Identifier Number (US), NDC Number (Package), NDC Number (Product), and Treatments Information dictionaries.
National Institute of Standards and Technology Risk Management Framework for Department of Defense IT (NIST RMF for DoD IT)
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.

The following engines are designed to detect National Institute of Standards and Technology Risk Management Framework for Department of Defense IT violations, using the Credit Cards, Diseases Information, Drugs Information, Social Security Numbers (US), Names (US), and Medical Information dictionaries:
High Volume:NIST (RMF for Dod IT) violations at a high threshold (i.e., more than 25 matches).
Low Volume: NIST (RMF for Dod IT) violations at a low threshold (i.e., more than one match).
Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA)
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.
The following engines are designed to detect Personal Data Protection Act violations, using the NRIC Numbers (Singapore) and Credit Cards dictionaries:
High Volume: PDPA violations at a high threshold (i.e., more than 25 matches).
Low Volume: PDPA violations at a low threshold (i.e., more than one match).
Personally Identifiable Inforamtion (PII) (US)
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.
The following engines are designed to detect Personally Identifiable Information violations, using the Social Security Numbers (US) and Tax Identification Number (US) dictionaries:
High Volume: PII (US) violations at a high threshold (i.e., more than 25 matches).
Low Volume: PII (US) violations at a low threshold (i.e., more than one match).
Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act (PIPEDA)
This engine is available by default for customers with tenants enabled on April 4, 2025, or later. To request access to these engines, contact Zscaler Support.

The following engines detect Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act violations, using the Names (Canada), Social Insurance Number (Canada), ABA Bank Routing Number, and Credit Cards dictionaries:
High Volume: PIPEDA violations at a high threshold (i.e., more than 25 matches).
Low Volume: PIPEDA violations at a low threshold (i.e., more than one match).

blocks.text: You can edit a predefined DLP engine to detect content that is relevant to your organization. To edit a predefined DLP engine:
You can also add a custom DLP engine. To learn more, see Adding Custom DLP Engines.

blocks.item: Go to Data Security > Common Resources > DLP Dictionaries & Engines > DLP Engines.
In the DLP Engines tab, click the Edit icon for the predefined DLP engine.

blocks.text: The Edit DLP Engine window appears.

blocks.item: For Channels, select the channels to which the engine applies. Excluding a channel can reduce the extra noise that comes from engines being used unnecessarily. When editing a DLP engine, you must select a channel.
You can optionally override the channels associated with an engine directly from the DLP Engines page:
On the DLP Engines page, select the checkbox next to an engine in the list.
You can't remove a channel from an engine that is used in an active policy.
In the Actions drop-down menu, select the channels to apply to the engine from the Select drop-down menu.
See image.
Click Apply.
The icons in the Channel column are updated to reflect the override setting.
For Engine Builder, add operators and DLP dictionaries to build an expression. You can see your expression in the Expression Preview.
See image.

Select an operator to build your expression. The operators include All (AND), Any (OR), Exclude (AND NOT), and Sum. The Sum operator is available for count-based DLP dictionaries (i.e., Credit Cards, Social Security Numbers, etc.) and allows you to specify the sum total of matches that trigger a group of dictionaries specified in the DLP engine.

blocks.text: For the root expression, only the All (AND), Any (OR), and Sum operators are allowed.

blocks.item: Click Add to add a Dictionary or a Subexpression. Click the Remove icon () to delete dictionaries or subexpressions.
If you use the Sum operator, select two or more predefined or custom DLP dictionaries. You must set a value for the match count. You can enter any value less than 1,000.

If you use the All, Any, or Exclude operators, you must select a predefined or custom DLP dictionary. Certain dictionaries require you to set a value for the match count. You can enter any value less than 1,000.
See image.

If you click Subexpression, you must select an operator. The operators include All (AND), Any (OR), Exclude (AND NOT), and Sum. The Sum operator is available for count-based DLP dictionaries (i.e., Credit Cards, Social Security Numbers, etc.) and allows you to specify the sum total of matches that trigger a group of dictionaries specified in the subexpression.

blocks.text: You can use the Sum operator as part of a subexpression; however, you cannot add a subexpression to an expression or subexpression that uses the Sum operator.

blocks.item: Continue adding dictionaries and operators to the expression as needed. At each level, you can create up to 4 subexpressions, use up to 4 operators, and add up to 16 dictionaries per operator.
Click Save and activate the change.
